metadata.name: [GCP Cloud Run OTel] High memory utilization by service
metadata.description: Fires when the p95 per-instance memory utilisation of a Cloud Run service is 85% or higher over a 30-minute window. Instances that exceed the memory limit are OOM-killed, which causes HTTP 500s and cold starts.

query.base:
TS metrics-gcp.cloudrun.otel-*
// Services only: cloud_run_job documents have no service_name
| WHERE `metrics.run.googleapis.com/container/memory/utilizations` IS NOT NULL
  AND resource.attributes.service_name IS NOT NULL
// Utilisation is a fraction 0-1 of the memory limit (in-memory filesystem writes count against it)
| STATS
    memory_p95 = PERCENTILE(`metrics.run.googleapis.com/container/memory/utilizations`::exponential_histogram, 95),
    memory_samples = COUNT(`metrics.run.googleapis.com/container/memory/utilizations`::exponential_histogram)
  BY resource.attributes.project_id, resource.attributes.location, resource.attributes.service_name

breach.segment:
// Minimum sample guard: ignore services that ran only briefly in the window
WHERE memory_samples >= 5
| EVAL memory_p95_pct = ROUND(memory_p95 * 100.0, 1)
// Alert threshold in percent (healthy services stay below ~70%)
| WHERE memory_p95_pct >= 85.0
| KEEP resource.attributes.project_id, resource.attributes.location, resource.attributes.service_name,
    memory_p95_pct, memory_samples
| SORT memory_p95_pct DESC
| LIMIT 50

data.content:
## Cloud Run high memory utilisation

The p95 per-instance memory utilisation was 85% or higher over the last 30 minutes. Instances that exceed their memory limit are terminated (OOM). In-flight requests then fail with HTTP 500s and the replacement instances cold-start.

### Triage
1. Check the 5xx error rate (500 responses) and startup latency for the same service. These confirm whether OOM kills are already happening. Container logs show the memory-limit termination message.
2. Check whether usage climbs steadily (a leak) or tracks traffic (per-request memory multiplied by concurrency).
3. Writes to the in-memory filesystem (`/tmp`) count against the memory limit. Check for growing temporary files.
4. Check for a new revision (`resource.attributes.revision_name`) with a higher memory footprint.
5. Remediate by raising the memory limit, lowering per-instance concurrency, or fixing the leak.

### Caveats
- The configured memory limit is not in the telemetry. Utilisation is relative to whatever limit is set.

### Tuning
- Adjust `memory_p95_pct >= 85.0`. Use a lower value for an earlier warning, but keep it above your normal steady state (healthy services usually stay below 70%).
- Adjust the `memory_samples >= 5` guard.
